question: What changed in the EU AI Act implementation timeline?
title: Changes to the EU AI Act Implementation Timeline

sentences.text: The EU AI Act entered into force on 1 August 2024, with general prohibitions taking effect on 2 February 2025 and obligations for general-purpose AI models applying from 2 August 2025.

Although the original deadline for high-risk AI rules was 2 August 2026, the timeline for enforcement was extended by the AI Omnibus to 2 December 2027 for stand-alone high-risk systems and 2 August 2028 for high-risk AI embedded in products.

In addition, the deadline for providers to implement transparency solutions for artificially generated content was set to 2 December 2026, and a prohibition on non-consensual intimate content takes effect in December 2026.
The EU AI Act officially entered into force on 1 August 2024, and prohibitions on prohibited AI practices took effect on 2 February 2025.
Obligations and rules for providers of general-purpose AI models became applicable on 2 August 2025.
The application deadline for stand-alone high-risk AI systems was delayed from the original date of 2 August 2026 to 2 December 2027.
The deadline for the enforcement of high-risk AI systems embedded in products was extended to 2 August 2028.
The grace period for providers to implement transparency solutions for artificially generated content was adjusted to a deadline of 2 December 2026.
A prohibition on AI systems generating or manipulating non-consensual intimate content comes into effect on 2 December 2026.
The deadline for national competent authorities to establish AI regulatory sandboxes was postponed to 2 August 2027.
The EU AI Act implementation schedule preserved its initial milestones for prohibited practices and general-purpose AI models while significantly extending high-risk compliance deadlines.

k1.statement: The EU AI Act officially entered into force on 1 August 2024.

k2.statement: The prohibited AI practices listed as 1-8 became effective in February 2025.

k3.statement: The regulatory rules for General-Purpose AI (GPAI) models became effective in August 2025.

k4.statement: Rules for high-risk AI systems used in certain high-risk areas (including biometrics, critical infrastructure, education, employment, migration, asylum and border control) will apply from 2 December 2027.

k5.statement: Rules for high-risk AI systems integrated into products (such as lifts or toys) will apply from 2 August 2028.

k6.statement: Prohibition 9, regarding non-consensual sexually explicit and intimate content, comes into effect in December 2026.

k7.statement: The EU AI Act was adopted in June 2024.

k8.statement: The deadline for transparency obligations regarding synthetic content for AI systems placed on the market before 2 August 2026 is postponed from 2 August 2026 to 2 December 2026.

k9.statement: The obligation for Member States to establish at least one national regulatory sandbox is postponed from 2 August 2026 to 2 August 2027.

k10.statement: A new prohibition on AI systems generating or manipulating non-consensual intimate imagery and CSAM takes effect on 2 December 2026.

k11.statement: General provisions and prohibitions of the EU AI Act apply starting 2 February 2025.

k12.statement: Rules for general-purpose AI and governance requirements apply from 2 August 2025.

k13.statement: Rules for high-risk AI systems in Annex III apply starting 2 December 2027.

k14.statement: Rules for high-risk AI embedded in regulated products covered by Annex I apply starting 2 August 2028.

k15.statement: The implementation timeline of the EU AI Act includes amendments introduced by the Digital Omnibus on AI.

k16.statement: The EU AI Act regulation generally applies from 2 August 2026, subject to certain exceptions.

k17.statement: The Commission is mandated to evaluate and report on the regulation for the first time by 2 August 2028, and every four years thereafter.

k18.statement: The prohibition of certain AI practices, including social scoring, subliminal manipulation, and real-time biometric remote identification in public spaces, has been in effect since February 2, 2025.

k19.statement: Transparency obligations under Art. 50 AI Act apply from August 2, 2026.

k20.statement: The ban on prohibited practices has been enforceable since February 2, 2025.

k21.statement: Obligations for general-purpose AI (GPAI) providers became enforceable on August 2, 2025.

k22.statement: Stand-alone high-risk AI systems have a new compliance deadline of December 2, 2027.

k23.statement: High-risk AI systems embedded in medical products have a new compliance deadline of August 2, 2028.

k24.statement: The European Parliament has voted to delay compliance deadlines for high-risk AI systems to December 2027.

k25.statement: The European Parliament has voted to push sector-specific obligations under the EU AI Act to August 2028.

k26.statement: To ensure the proposed delay takes legal effect, a political agreement must be reached in the Council of the European Union, likely before June 2026.

k27.statement: The EU AI Act has banned AI systems that could threaten people's safety as of February 2025.

k28.statement: Providers of General Purpose AI (GPAI) systems released after August 2, 2025, must comply with the EU AI Act's provisions.

k29.statement: Operators of high-risk AI systems must be compliant with the EU AI Act by August 2026.

k30.statement: The European Commission has explicitly rejected industry calls for enforcement pauses, confirming that there are no delays to the implementation timeline.

k31.statement: The General-Purpose AI Code of Practice was published on July 10, 2025.

k32.statement: For GPAI models, the EU Commission will enforce all obligations and may impose fines for noncompliance starting on 2 August 2026.

k33.statement: The AI Office will recognize good-faith efforts to achieve compliance for GPAI providers starting on 2 August 2025 rather than viewing them as having breached commitments under the Code of Practice.

k34.statement: The EU AI Act rules regarding General-Purpose AI (GPAI) models apply starting from 2 August 2025.

k35.statement: The General-Purpose AI (GPAI) code of practice was published on July 10, 2025.

k36.statement: The original application date for obligations regarding high-risk AI systems was set for August 2.

k37.statement: The European Parliament proposed a new application date of December 2, 2027, for specifically listed high-risk AI systems.

k38.statement: The European Parliament proposed a new application date of August 2, 2028, for AI systems covered by EU sectoral legislation on safety and market surveillance.

k39.statement: The European Parliament proposed a compliance deadline of November 2, 2026, for rules requiring watermarking of AI-created content.

k40.statement: GPAI model rules and governance structures became operative on August 2, 2025.

k41.statement: Annex III high-risk AI system obligations are set to take effect on August 2, 2026.

k42.statement: The European Commission proposed the Digital Omnibus (COM(2025) 836) to delay the Annex III high-risk deadline to December 2, 2027.

k43.statement: The Digital Omnibus proposal (COM(2025) 836) aims to delay the Annex I high-risk deadline to December 2, 2028.

k44.statement: The final version of the Transparency Code of Practice for AI-Generated Content (Article 50) is expected in June 2026.

k45.statement: The transparency obligations under Article 50 of the AI Act for providers and deployers of generative AI systems become applicable on 2 August 2026.

k46.statement: The final Code of Practice on transparency of AI-generated content was published on 10 June 2026.

k47.statement: Obligations for providers of General-Purpose AI (GPAI) models under the EU AI Act take effect starting August 2, 2025.

k48.statement: Obligations for providers of general-purpose AI models under the AI Act entered into application on 2 August 2025.

k49.statement: The Commission's enforcement powers regarding obligations for providers of GPAI models enter into application on 2 August 2026.

k50.statement: Providers of general-purpose AI models placed on the market before 2 August 2025 must comply with obligations by 2 August 2027.

k51.statement: The original date for the entry into application of high-risk AI rules was 2 August 2026.

k52.statement: The timeline for the enforcement of high-risk AI systems has been extended to 2 December 2027 by the AI Omnibus.

k53.statement: The timeline for the enforcement of AI embedded in products has been extended to 2 August 2028 by the AI Omnibus.

k54.statement: CEN and CENELEC were requested to develop standards for high-risk AI requirements by August 2025 but failed to do so.

k55.statement: The original deadline for the application of provisions on high-risk AI systems was 2 August 2026.

k56.statement: The new application deadline for stand-alone high-risk AI systems is 2 December 2027.

k57.statement: The new application deadline for high-risk AI systems embedded in products is 2 August 2028.

k58.statement: The deadline for the establishment of AI regulatory sandboxes by national competent authorities is postponed until 2 August 2027.

k59.statement: The grace period for providers to implement transparency solutions for artificially generated content is reduced, with a new deadline of 2 December 2026.

k60.statement: The deadline for stand-alone high-risk AI systems is delayed to 2 December 2027.

k61.statement: The deadline for high-risk AI systems embedded in products is delayed to 2 August 2028.

k62.statement: The deadline for the establishment of AI regulatory sandboxes by national competent authorities is postponed to 2 December 2027.

k63.statement: The new deadline for providers to implement transparency solutions for artificially generated content is 2 December 2026.

k64.statement: The procedural vehicle for the changes to the AI Act timeline is the "Omnibus VII" legislative package.
